business_scope.primary_industry_name: Statutory Company Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 June regulating the beneficial ownership information register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid Passport or National Identity Card
Certificate of Incorporation or Equivalent from Foreign Entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against EU PEP lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, and Spanish domestic sanctions lists in full compliance with AMLD5/6 standards

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of Spanish language and Latin script; no transliteration required
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: terms reserved for regulated financial or public entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal (recurso potestativo de reposición) within one month to the Registrar before the Commercial Registry; judicial review available under Ley 39/2015 del Procedimiento Administrativo Común if necessary

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted and standard for SL companies; registered office may be a virtual address provided by authorized service providers
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; unannounced inspections rare (estimated <5% probability) and typically limited to specific AML or tax audits

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee plus prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and mail forwarding
Legal due diligence and incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO and PEP screening and compliance setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20-23, 31-35, 62, 78-79, 159-161, 210-212, 214-215, and 279-281; Commercial Registry Regulation approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) under the Ministry of Justice and supervised administratively through the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the corporate name certificate and tax identification application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 in equity, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. A bank escrow account and bank certificate are not generally mandatory where the incorporation deed records the founders' joint and several liability for the existence and payment of the contributions; a bank certificate is customary for cash contributions. Contributions in kind require proper description and valuation in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The directors resolve that: (1) the Company accepts and records the subscription and full payment of the shares stated in the deed of incorporation; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address specified in the deed, with authority granted to update it within the statutory limits; (3) [Name] is appointed sole director, or the persons named in the deed are appointed as directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) [Name] is appointed secretary, if a board structure is used; and (5) the directors are authorized to complete all tax, registry, banking, AML, employment, and municipal filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online or signed application for a negative name certificate, listing permitted alternative names. Ensure the proposed name includes the legal form or its accepted abbreviation, S.L. The certificate must generally be valid for three months for incorporation purposes and may be renewed within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Proposed company names in priority order
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Foreign shareholder identification documents, legalized or apostilled and translated where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name or challenge the refusal through the Registry's available administrative or judicial review channels. Correct identity, power-of-attorney, or translation defects before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Corporate and Beneficial Ownership Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, ownership schedule, management structure, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, contribution details, and beneficial ownership information. Obtain apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translations for foreign corporate documents. Verify directors' tax identification numbers and powers of representation.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports or national identity documents
Foreign shareholders' certificates of incorporation, constitutional documents, incumbency evidence, and powers of attorney
Beneficial ownership declaration and ownership chart
Evidence of registered office or address authorization
Bank certificate for cash contributions, if used
In-kind contribution descriptions and supporting valuation documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial observations by correcting the articles, providing missing legalized documents, or replacing defective powers of attorney. Obtain a new name certificate if the existing certificate expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders or duly empowered representatives sign the public deed. The deed must state the identity of founders, contributions, subscribed shares, articles, initial management, and beneficial ownership information. The notary verifies identity, capacity, powers, foreign-document formalities, and applicable anti-money-laundering information.
required_dossiers: Original or electronically verifiable negative name certificate
Capital contribution evidence or statutory liability declaration
Foreign-document apostilles or legalizations and sworn translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify the deed by notarial correction or execute a supplemental deed. If the notary refuses authorization, obtain written grounds and submit corrected documentation or seek applicable professional and judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the provisional NIF using Form 036 and submit the notarial deed for electronic or physical registration with the Provincial Commercial Registry. Pay applicable notarial and registry charges. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF and update the Tax Agency with the registered deed and final corporate data.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder tax identification evidence, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Registry's nota de calificación by correcting the identified defect within the permitted period, filing a supplemental deed where required, or appealing under the Commercial Registry review procedure. Correct tax-form inconsistencies through an amended Form 036.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Corporate Governance and Compliance Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry, Spanish Tax Agency, Social Security General Treasury, and the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offences (SEPBLAC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalize mandatory accounting and corporate books electronically through the Commercial Registry. Obtain a qualified electronic certificate. Register employees, if any, with Social Security. Because professional company-secretarial, registered-office, nominee, or related services may constitute services to companies under Law 10/2010, assess and, where applicable, register the provider in the Commercial Registry's register of providers of services to companies and implement SEPBLAC AML controls.
required_dossiers: Corporate books and accounting-book legalization request
AML risk assessment, policies, customer-due-diligence procedures, and beneficial ownership records
Provider-registration filing, where the activity falls within Law 10/2010
Employment and Social Security documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic filings, resubmit defective book files, and answer SEPBLAC or Registry information requests. Maintain documented remediation and escalation procedures for AML registration or compliance deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Municipal Premises and Activity Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the office is located, with the relevant autonomous-community authority where sectoral approval applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm zoning compatibility for the office and determine whether the activity requires a prior operating or activity licence, responsible declaration, communication of commencement, works permit, accessibility certificate, or signage approval. File the applicable municipal procedure before commencing activity and retain proof of submission.
required_dossiers: Technical activity memorandum or project, if required
Proof of municipal taxes and fees, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure municipal technical observations, obtain revised plans or certificates, and resubmit. Use the applicable administrative appeal against an express refusal; do not commence a regulated activity before the required licence or effective responsible-declaration period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single national industrial licensing board applies to ordinary corporate-secretarial or registered-agent offices. The competent authorities are the relevant Ayuntamiento for premises and activity authorization, and the autonomous-community industry authority for any regional technical, installation, or regulated-activity approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal activity or opening licence (licencia de actividad o apertura), or responsible declaration/communication of commencement (declaración responsable o comunicación previa), depending on the municipality and premises classification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from formal EIA for a normal office-based corporate-secretarial or registered-agent activity with no industrial installations, material emissions, or significant environmental impact. A municipal environmental screening or compatibility declaration may still be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater, VOC, or process-emission limits ordinarily apply to a standard office. The company must comply with municipal sewer rules, waste separation and transfer requirements, and applicable commercial or hazardous-waste rules. Any printer chemicals, batteries, electronic waste, or cleaning substances must be handled through authorized channels. An industrial discharge, generator, storage installation, or material emissions source may trigger regional permits and sector-specific limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal fire-safety and occupancy compliance where required, including emergency routes, extinguishers, electrical safety, accessibility, and maximum occupancy. Structural load certification is required only where the premises, equipment, alteration, or use creates a technical trigger. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, including risk assessment, preventive planning, worker information and training, and health surveillance through an authorized prevention service. A standalone national workplace-clearance certificate is not generally required for a conventional office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica, https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an incorporated Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the notary applies for a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) at the time of deed execution. Once the SL is registered in the Mercantile Registry, the definitive NIF is ratified through Form 036 (Declaración censal) filed electronically with AEAT. The same Form 036 effects simultaneous registration in the Spanish VAT census (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) and the business activity census. For a non-resident foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Spain, AEAT assigns a non-resident NIF under Form 036/037 and may require the appointment of a fiscal representative resident in Spain where the entity is established outside the EU/EEA, in accordance with Article 45 of Ley 58/2003.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The ES_SL is a resident corporate entity subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide income at the general rate of 25%. No pass-through treatment is available under Spanish domestic law; the entity is a separate taxpayer from its shareholders. Non-resident shareholders receiving dividends or transfers are separately subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Spanish tax law; the SL's corporate status is non-elective. Available elections include: (i) VAT group registration (Régimen de Grupo de Entidades, art. 163 quarterdecies Ley 37/1992) for entities under common control; (ii) corporate income tax consolidation (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal, arts. 61–103 Ley 27/2014) for groups that meet the 50%+ control and equity thresholds; (iii) provisional tax payment options under IS; and (iv) designation of deemed fixed establishment or fiscal representative for VAT. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply mandatorily, with no positive election to alter the entity's characterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA). Ley 37/1992 and Royal Decree 1624/1992.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold for resident companies. An SL must register for Spanish VAT before carrying out the first taxable supply. For intra-EU distance sales of goods into Spain by another EU established supplier, the registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year via the OSS scheme. The Spanish simplified VAT regime (Régimen Simplificado) may apply to certain individual businesses with turnover below EUR 250,000, but it is not relevant to a usual corporate secretarial services SL.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain operates the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) regime requiring VAT-registered businesses with turnover above EUR 6,010,121.40 or those under certain large-taxpayer schemes to submit invoice records and received-invoice records electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days of issuance or receipt. Under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), private-sector B2B electronic invoicing is mandatory for all companies and self-employed persons, using an interoperable solution; AEAT has established the Verifactura channel to receive and verify invoice data from electronic invoicing solution providers on a near-real-time basis. Public sector e-invoicing through Facturae has been mandatory since 2015.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exención plena) applies under Ley 37/1992 art. 21 to exports of goods physically leaving the European Union, provided the exporter proves the exit of the goods within 3 months from supply, retains the relevant shipping and customs documentation, and records the import or entry into the destination. Intra-EU dispatches to taxable customers under art. 25 are exempt subject to valid Spanish VAT ID of the supplier and the customer's intra-community VAT number; reverse charge applies to the customer. For offshore secretarial and registered-agent services supplied to a business customer outside Spain, the general B2B place-of-supply rule in art. 69 LIVA places the supply where the customer is established, so the service is outside the scope of Spanish VAT, no Spanish VAT being charged; if the customer is established outside the EU the service is subject to Spanish VAT only where the customer is a non-taxable person within the meaning of art. 84. A written declaration, the customer's VAT ID or equivalent tax identification, and proof of external establishment are required to substantiate the non-application of Spanish VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) accepted and validated by Spanish Customs
Bill of Lading (or CMR/CIM/Air Waybill) evidencing physical exit from Spain and the European Union
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 proof of receipt of export sales proceeds
Commercial invoice, packing list, export sales contract, and Incoterms evidence
VAT registration certificate of the supplier and, where applicable, the customer's intra-EU VAT identification number or foreign tax identification number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT and Spanish Customs may retrospectively deny zero-rating or non-application of VAT where export documentation is deficient, falsified, or incomplete, with resulting assessment of Spanish VAT plus default interest and surcharges. Proportional tax penalties under Ley 58/2003 art. 184 may range from 50% to 150% of the tax base, and serious infringements may trigger loss of deductions and publication of penalties. If the omitted or evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, a criminal offense against the Government Treasury (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) can apply to legal representatives. Additionally, false statements in the SII and electronic invoicing framework may give rise to separate administrative sanctions under Ley 18/2022, with fines for non-compliance with electronic invoicing obligations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the European System of Central Banks and under the European Central Bank for euro monetary policy; foreign-exchange surveillance in Spain is shared between Banco de España and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) for balance-of-payments reporting and foreign-investment registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Spain applies no exchange-control permit regime under Articles 63–66 TFEU; capital movements are unrestricted except for EU autonomous financial sanctions, anti-money-laundering holds, and sectoral foreign-direct-investment screening under Regulation (EU) 2019/452 and Law 19/2003. A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may receive 100% non-resident shareholding without prior central-bank authorization. Post-closing ex-post declarations to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (R.I.E.) are mandatory for non-EU investors acquiring direct control or >10% equity; the statutory Form D-1A is due within one month of the notarized capital injection. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders encounter no currency-conversion barrier, but Spanish withholding tax of 19% (reduced under applicable double-tax treaties; 20% for non-cooperative jurisdictions) applies on dividends, with Form 216 filing and the payment executed only after presentation of the beneficiary tax-residence certificate and the dividend-resolution minutes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline on export receipts. For the SL's registered-agent service fees, the regime is purely statistical: under Banco de España Circular 4/2012, any foreign receipt or payment exceeding €50,000 per declaration window (or €100,000 per single operation) must be reported electronically via the 'Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior' system within 30 days after month-end, using balance-of-payments code 2060 for business/secretarial services. The documentary baseline comprises signed service contracts, invoice registers, and, for goods-linked flows, the customs DUA declaration; records must be retained for at least five years for AML, tax, and statistical audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (cuenta de integración de capital) for Art. 62 LSC deposit certificate plus multi-currency Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account; dedicated FX desk for forwards and NDFs; strong LatAm correspondent coverage
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account; SEPA-instant and MT103 corridors for Iberian-American payment flows
Operational Account; international boutique desk for service-sector SMEs and non-resident director structures
Operational Account; premium relationship banking with discretionary acceptance of offshore-adjacent corporate services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for ancillary operational liquidity (SEPA collections, EUR MT103-equivalent outflows, card acquiring) through EU-licensed electronic money institutions such as Qonto, Revolut Business, N26 Business, and Bnext; Low and legally excluded for statutory capital escrow because the notary's certificado bancario under Article 62 Ley de Sociedades de Capital must be issued by a credit institution authorized under Spanish Law 10/2014 — an EMI passport under PSD2 cannot issue it. Additional constraints: EMIs are not admitted to TARGET2, cannot hold the capital deposit as blocked funds, and typically cap balances and card velocity; they are acceptable solely as secondary float accounts for client-fee liquidity not exceeding €50,000, with daily sweeping to a Tier 1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Law 10/2010 (amended by Law 6/2023) and eIDAS, remote onboarding is legally permissible using a qualified electronic signature and video-identity verification. In practice, Tier 1 Spanish banks exercise underwriting discretion: where all directors and shareholders are non-resident and the SL's declared purpose is offshore secretarial services, banks typically require at least one of (a) an in-branch interview with the sole director, (b) an apostilled notarized power of attorney attested at a Spanish consulate, or (c) a live video call with the compliance officer plus certified passport copies. Where no director holds an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero), banks ordinarily mandate a provisional NIE application or appointment of a Spanish tax representative before opening the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial-owner chain using opaque intermediates (trusts, foundations, offshore-company layers) holding 100% of the SL's quota shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory UBO register (Titularidad Real) naming each ultimate natural person; legalized corporate organigram of all intermediate entities; foreign certificate of good standing; notarized Libro Registro de Socios; sworn source-of-wealth statement with six months of shareholder bank statements; tax-residence certificates of each intermediate entity; written explanation of economic rationale for the intermediate layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-model red flag: registered-agent and offshore secretarial services inherently create the risk of facilitating third-party shell structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CFT policy (art. 24 Ley 10/2010) detailing client intake, refusal lists for sanctioned and non-cooperative jurisdictions, and continuous transaction monitoring; appointment of an independent external AML officer; professional-indemnity insurance policy; complete client due-diligence files (expedientes de identificación) evidencing underlying UBO, commercial purpose, and service contract for every third-party client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an unrelated third-party shareholder or lender with no auditable nexus to the SL's structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original notarial incorporation deed containing the bank's blocked-deposit certificate under Art. 62 LSC; fund-origin letter from the remitting bank; investor board resolution approving the contribution; Form D-1A filed with the R.I.E.; undertaking to provide source-of-funds evidence for all subsequent aportaciones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring cross-border outbound wires (especially to Latin America) inconsistent with the declared operational scale of a secretarial firm.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with each counterparty; invoice-and-deliverable reconciliation ledger; mapping of every outbound MT103 to a KYC-verified client file; Model 349/347 tax declarations where intra-EU thresholds apply; treasury policy mandating exclusive bank-rail settlement (SEPA/MT103) and prohibiting cash, bearer instruments, and unstructured person-to-person transfers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 (non-EUR) or SEPA credit transfer (EUR) with Field 70/Remittance Information reading 'Aportación capital social ES_SL – Escritura [date]', and the bank's balance-of-payments statistical code 701 (inversión directa en sociedad no cotizada) attached. Funds are blocked in the capital-integration escrow until the Notary executes the deed and the Registro Mercantil registers the SL; subsequent share-premium or shareholder-loan inflows use code 701 or 702L and require a board resolution plus source-of-funds evidence. Non-EU investors must file Form D-1A with the R.I.E. within one month; failure to declare triggers administrative fines. Verification bundle: notarial certificate, deposit certificate, UBO disclosure, and the contributor's bank confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (a) SWIFT MT103 for international fiat payments (fee notes to registered-agent clients, correspondent-agent commissions, procurement of legalization services), with supporting invoice and KYC file; (b) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated intra-EU payments settling via EBA CLEARING/TARGET2 in T+1; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700) for high-value service-procurement contracts exceeding €100,000; (d) MT202 COV strictly for financial-institution intermediary legs — never for direct client payments. Each disbursement above €10,000 triggers Banco de España statistical declaration and enhanced fraud-scoring; the counterparty KYC file, signed service attestation, and, where applicable, intra-group service agreement must be archived.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (plain vanilla) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF with tenors up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with an investment-grade Spanish dealer

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible Latin American currencies — EUR/ARS, EUR/BRL, EUR/MXN, EUR/CLP — cash-settled in EUR against reference fixings, permissible only where a matching trade receivable or payables exposure exists

Cross-Currency Swaps (FX swaps) for temporary conversion of EUR into USD or GBP to cover short-term liquidity gaps, with same-day or next-value settlement and prohibition of speculative position-taking

Optional FX options (European-style, zero-premium structures) on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP, subject to board-approved treasury policy, independent valuation at mark-to-market, and EMIR transaction reporting; the medium-risk SL remains a non-financial counterparty below clearing thresholds (NFC-) and benefits from the clearing exemption, though portfolio reconciliation and dual-sided EMIR reporting apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) and, where applicable, directors' report/audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholders’ approval; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year entities must present by 30 June of the following year and deposit by no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: First-year delinquency blocks further registrations and requires auditor appointment; continuing default for one year closes the registry folio; two consecutive years without deposit triggers an administrative closure and strike-off risk, in addition to possible fines and impossibility to file merger/liquidation deeds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 days following the six-month post-close window; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 20% (or fixed 20% after 12 months), statutory late-payment interest, and penalty surcharges from 50% to 150% where the return is filed after AEAT formal notice; non-filing of taxes exceeding EUR 120,000 carries criminal tax exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 January of the calendar year immediately following the tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same general surcharge regime under Article 27 of the Ley General Tributaria: 1% per month up to 20%, statutory interest, plus penalties up to 150% of omitted quota; the omission of the annual summary may also constitute a separate formal infringement proceeding.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: total assets EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover EUR 5,700,000; average headcount greater than 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory when required by parent-group consolidation or upon holders of at least 5% of share capital making a timely request under the Spanish Audit Law 22/2015.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Royal Decree 1514/2007, as amended), derived from the Código de Comercio; IFRS applies to consolidated financial statements of groups subject to Regulation (EC) 1606/2002 but is not the default framework for individual statutory accounts of a non-listed S.L.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Ley 10/2010 the S.L. must hold and update an internal Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales). At the ordinary general meeting approving the annual accounts, the board or corporate secretary issues a written UBO confirmation to the shareholders; any change in shareholders or effective control is stamped in the register and reflected in the public accounts. Non-resident or foreign transferors are also subject to post-closing notarial filing at the Registro Mercantil and to Form DP-2 foreign-investment statistical filing where the regulated ownership thresholds apply. The register is available for inspection by SEBLAC/FIU and must be certified by the registered agent at each annual maintenance review.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 700 – US$ 2,200 per annum (market range for Madrid/Barcelona corporate secretarial and registered office packages)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 3,200 – US$ 7,500 per annum for a small S.L. without consolidated accounting; wider range if IFRS/group audit or regulatory work is added

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base in the first two eligible tax periods; 100% deduction for qualifying R&D and IT personnel expenses; 50%-75% incentives for certain export and internationalisation activities; no general statutory tax holidays for registered agent services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed through the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) electronic portal; mandatory electronic submission for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), including fully foreign-owned entities, using a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; separate quarterly fractional prepayments are filed on Modelo 220 in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the tax year end; for a fiscal year ending 31 December, the statutory deadline is 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number and fiscal name of the Spanish SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the definitive Spanish NIF of the SL; a non-resident owner cannot be inserted in this block. If NIF is pending, provide the provisional number and file a rectification later.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary business activity classified under the Spanish CNAE-2009 code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select CNAE 8299 for general business support services or CNAE 6910 when legal and corporate secretarial functions are also performed. The chosen code must reflect the true Spanish activity, not merely the offshore marketing description.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss for the tax period as stated in the SL's profit and loss account under Spanish GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The full worldwide income of the SL is reported here because the SL is tax-resident in Spain. Non-resident shareholders' residence does not reduce this amount; international transactions must be reflected in the financial statements at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after permanent and temporary adjustments, prior-year loss offset, and elimination of exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments and economic substance arguments are evaluated at this line. Loss carryforward is applied under the administrative assumption of the five-year template; if the taxpayer relies on Spanish law's unlimited carryforward, attach a formal position paper with cited case law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full corporate income tax liability at 25% before deductions, prepayments, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL computes tax as a Spanish resident; treaty benefits claimed by non-resident shareholders are not deductible from the SL's corporate tax. Only the SL's own foreign tax credits and statutory incentives are allowed here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount to be paid to or refunded by the AEAT after deducting fractional prepayments and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds are paid into the SL's Spanish bank account, not to foreign shareholders. If the SL has no residual payment due as a result of tax credits, include full supporting schedules in the filing packet.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharges under LGT Arts. 27 and 61.3: 5% if filed within three months of the deadline; 10% if within six months; 15% if within twelve months; 20% if later, plus late-payment interest. Incorrect or omitted returns causing underpayment trigger LGT Art. 191 penalties of 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, with increased sanctions for deliberate or intransparent conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory non-resident dividend withholding rate is 19% for shareholders resident in EU/EEA states with administrative co-operation mechanisms and 24% for shareholders resident outside those frameworks. Qualifying EU parent companies may apply 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when holding at least 5% for an uninterrupted 12-month period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend, royalty, or interest rate under a Double Taxation Agreement, the beneficial owner must lodge a Certificate of Tax Residence issued by the foreign tax authority with the Spanish paying SL before the payment date. The SL may apply the treaty rate at source on submission of the TRC and a statement of beneficial ownership. If tax was over-withheld, the non-resident must apply for a refund using Modelo 210 (or Modelo 212 in specific cases). EU parent-companies additionally file Modelo 296 to certify exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest paid to non-residents is 19% for EU/EEA information-exchange residents and 24% for other non-residents; royalties are 24% under the Spanish IRNR Act, with 19% only where an EU/EEA information-exchange treaty supports it. Relevant treaty rates vary: for many Spanish treaties interest is 10%, royalties are 5%-10%, and the EU Interest-Royalties Directive allows 0% on qualifying related-party cross-border interest and royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 of related-party transactions per related person in a tax period triggers mandatory Local File documentation; a Master File is required where the Spanish SL belongs to a multinational group with consolidated turnover above EUR 45 million in the preceding year. Even below these thresholds, related-party transactions must be valued at arm's length and Form 232 (annual related-party transaction report) is mandatory when the aggregate amount of controlled transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 per related party.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply the British-model Economic Substance Regulations applicable in offshore centres, but the Spanish system enforces genuine economic substance through general anti-abuse rules (LGT Art. 15), transfer pricing provisions (Art. 18 LIS), and ATAD anti-abuse measures. An SL engaged in registered agent and corporate secretarial work must maintain a real office, orderly statutory books, qualified persons performing management, or subcontractors under genuine contracts; otherwise the AEAT may disregard the arrangement and reattribute the Spanish-source income to the actual operators or to the non-resident beneficial owners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating the SL's taxable base by omitting secretarial fees, disguising non-deductible distributions to non-resident owners as commercial expenses, or using false cross-border invoices without real underlying services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: LGT Art. 191 penalty of 50% to 150% of the amount evaded plus late interest; criminal liability under Penal Code Art. 305 if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per taxable year, carrying imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount; loss of tax credits and carryforwards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under LGT Art. 42.2 when they caused the breach by wilful or negligent management. Signing knowingly false tax returns or instructing the suppression of income leads to criminal responsibility, travel bans, disqualification from managing Spanish companies, and personal confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating or promoting the Spanish SL purely as a tax shield without physical office, employees, independent management, or real business function; allowing a nominee director to act solely on non-resident instructions with no exercise of independent judgement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may declare the arrangement sham under LGT Art. 15, reallocate income to the material participants, and impose a 50%-150% penalty on the underlying tax avoided. The Mercantile Registry may also launch striking-off or dissolution procedures if the company lacks a real business object.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director lending their professional standing to a substance-less entity is personally liable under LGT Art. 42.1.b as participant in the tax avoidance; criminal penalties for collusion or document fraud are available, and courts frequently impose travel bans and seizure of assets while the hidden ownership structure is investigated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The registered-agent SL failing to perform customer due diligence on beneficial owners, omitting UBO filings, destroying records, or helping non-resident clients maintain anonymous Spanish corporate vehicles in breach of Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 10/2010 range from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious infringements and include temporary suspension of corporate activities; criminal money-laundering penalties of six months to six years imprisonment apply under Penal Code Art. 301 where the SL is used to move criminal or tax-evaded funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML-compliance officers are the natural addressees of the infraction; they face imprisonment, personal fines, travel bans, and disqualification from financial and corporate professions. Civil liability to clients and the State may also be asserted against the directors' personal estates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, maintain, or electronically file the Local File/Master File or Form 232 for controlled transactions with non-resident shareholders or affiliates; or pricing the SL's secretarial and agency services without an arm's-length benchmark so that Spanish operating profit is artificially depressed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under Art. 18 LIS of 15% on the amount of the undocumented or mispriced operation, with a minimum fine of EUR 3,000. The AEAT may additionally adjust the taxpayer's income under the arm's-length standard and charge late-payment interest; if the adjusted unpaid tax exceeds EUR 120,000 and is considered deliberate, the tax offence regime actively applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or managers who cause, sign, or tolerate false transfer-pricing documentation are jointly liable for the resulting tax debt under LGT Art. 42.2. In aggravated cases, they may be prosecuted under Penal Code Art. 305 for evasion, face imprisonment, travel restrictions, and be disqualified from acting as administrators of Spanish companies.
